newsitem.title: USA: U.S. machine tool demand fell sharply in January.
newsitem.headline: U.S. machine tool demand fell sharply in January.

text.p: U.S. demand for machine tools fell sharply in January to an estimated $649 million from a revised $739 million in December, the American Machine Tool Distributors' Association and the Association for Manufacturing Technology said Sunday in a joint report.
The January figure was down 12.2 percent from December. It was up three percent from the $630 million estimate for January 1996.
The December figure was revised from $839 million reported a month ago.
"Compared to January 1996, the year has begun on an upbeat note, with four of five regions reporting greater order strength," AMTDA President Ralph Nappi said in a statement.
"As the Midwest's and automotive markets' needs for capital acquisition level off, we now see a broader consumption balance across other industries and geographic areas," Nappi added.

The latest figures were from the eighth U.S. Machine Tool Consumption report which replaced monthly data on U.S. machine tool orders, shipments and exports issued by the Association for Manufacturing Technology. It is the first joint report containing a year-ago estimate for total demand.
Machine tools are used to shape metal in making everything from bicycles to aircraft. Demand for these tools can provide a leading indicator of the pace of manufacturing.
The report said 3,231 machine tool units were ordered in January. Units ordered in the previous and year-ago month were unavailable, but will be provided in the February report.

By region, the report said the Midwest accounted for about 41.9 percent of national demand, followed by 16.4 percent in both the Northeast and Central regions. The South accounted for 14.3 percent and the West about 11 percent, the report said.
Export orders placed with U.S. machine tool makers totaled 273 units in January, the report said.
